rows.name: Second Wind
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Sets the current CON regeneration feat-family contribution to 22% MaxHP and enables passive Health Regeneration if no other source already enabled it. After 5.0 continuous seconds without taking effective damage, regenerate at BaseHealthRegen = 1.0% MaxHP/second × ConRegenMultiplier toward the actor's final HealthRegenCeilingFraction. Regeneration stops when that ceiling is reached or effective damage is taken, never exceeds ordinary MaxHP, and never restores temporary Tetris overfill. This 22% feat contribution stacks additively with the Fighter's innate 33% contribution and any other independently authored additive regeneration-ceiling contributions.

rows.name: Venomous
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets PoisonProcChance = 0.55. On an eligible target-hit event under the common status-proc rules, a successful proc creates one poison-status application attempt using the attacker's CON for PoisonDC and the defender's CON for PoisonSave. A failed save applies the canonical Poisoned state; a successful save prevents it. Existing Poisoned reapplication/recovery rules remain authoritative.

rows.name: Toxic
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Venomous and sets PoisonProcChance = 0.75. All targeting, one-roll-per-target-hit, CON save, Poisoned reapplication, and non-stacking rules are unchanged.

rows.name: Virulent
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Toxic and sets PoisonProcChance = 0.95. All other Venomous-family semantics remain unchanged. PoisonStepDamage created later by this condition is status damage and can never itself roll this or any other offensive status-proc family.

rows.name: Glow Up
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI that already possess at least one explicit CHA_MOD-derived damage source
rows.effect: Whenever an owned rule would contribute max(0, CHA_MOD) as damage to a resolved damage event, Glow Up contributes GlowUpDamageBonus = max(0, CON_MOD) to that same event exactly once. This includes CHA-derived flat add-ons such as Aggressive Personality and Self-Actualization and CHA-derived damage events such as the Abrasive Personality family and Aura Burst family; future effects qualify only when their authored damage rule explicitly contributes CHA_MOD as damage. Glow Up never creates a damage event on its own, never adds CON_MOD more than once to the same resolved damage event even if multiple CHA-derived rules contribute to it, and does not alter damage dice, Boom behavior, Push, hit-stun, status-proc chance, Magic cost, Morale, or other riders. For ordinary player feat drafts and AI FeatDirector candidate construction, Glow Up is ineligible and must not be offered unless the actor already owns at least one currently usable CHA_MOD-derived damage rule; this dynamic prerequisite is checked before candidate weighting so Glow Up cannot appear as a dead pick. Losing or suppressing the qualifying effect later does not remove an already-owned Glow Up, but Glow Up simply contributes nothing while no qualifying CHA-derived damage is being produced.

rows.name: Rapid Recovery
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Replaces Second Wind's feat-family contribution and sets the current CON regeneration feat-family contribution to 44% MaxHP. After the same 5.0-second damage-free delay, regenerate at 1.5% MaxHP/second × ConRegenMultiplier toward the final ordinary Health-Regeneration ceiling. It does not stack with Second Wind inside the feat family, but this 44% feat contribution stacks additively with the Fighter's innate 33% contribution and any other independently authored additive regeneration-ceiling contributions. Never exceed ordinary MaxHP or restore temporary Tetris overfill.

rows.name: Unbroken
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Replaces lower Recovery ranks and sets the current CON regeneration feat-family contribution to 66% MaxHP. After the same 5.0-second damage-free delay, regenerate at 2.0% MaxHP/second × ConRegenMultiplier toward the final ordinary Health-Regeneration ceiling. Neither rate nor ceiling stacks with lower ranks inside the feat family. This 66% feat contribution stacks additively with the Fighter's innate 33% contribution and any other independently authored additive regeneration-ceiling contributions. The completed chain yields a 66% ceiling for a non-Fighter with no other source and a 99% ceiling for a Fighter before any other contribution. Never exceed ordinary MaxHP or restore temporary Tetris overfill; existing actor, boss and lifecycle exclusions remain unchanged.

rows.name: Perfect Ten
rows.actors: Non-Rogue heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with d10 damage rolls
rows.effect: The actor's ordinary player-owned/actor-owned d10 damage dice become exploding dice. A fresh d10 explodes only on natural 10. Continuation d10s use threshold max(2, 10 - BoomShift). Every explosion adds another d10 to the same damage chain and is subject to the universal 32-die safety cap.

rows.name: Distracting
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets ClumsyProcChance = 0.55. On an eligible target-hit event under the common status-proc rules, a successful proc creates one clumsy-tagged application attempt using the attacker's DEX for ClumsyDC and the defender's DEX for ClumsySave. A failed save applies canonical Clumsy; a successful save prevents it.

rows.name: Disorienting
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Distracting and sets ClumsyProcChance = 0.75. All common status-proc aggregation, save, duration, and non-stacking rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Discombobulating
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Disorienting and sets ClumsyProcChance = 0.95. All other Distracting-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend canonical Clumsy according to its existing later-expiration rule and never compound its movement/spread multipliers.

rows.name: Singeing
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets ImmolateProcChance = 0.55. On an eligible target-hit under the shared Status-proc feat-family rules, a successful proc creates exactly one Immolated application attempt using the attacker's DEX for ImmolateDC and the defender's DEX for ImmolateSave. A successful save prevents ignition. If that attack already guarantees an Immolated save through an authored fire/immolate rule, skip this redundant proc roll.

rows.name: Scorching
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Singeing and sets ImmolateProcChance = 0.75. All other Singeing-family semantics remain unchanged.

rows.name: Incendiary
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Scorching and sets ImmolateProcChance = 0.95. All other Singeing-family semantics remain unchanged; Immolated never stacks parallel tick streams and follows its canonical stored-DC/later-expiration reapplication rule.

rows.name: Eight Is Enough
rows.actors: Non-Rogue heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with d8 damage rolls
rows.effect: The actor's ordinary d8 damage dice become exploding dice. A fresh d8 explodes only on natural 8. Continuation d8s use threshold max(2, 8 - BoomShift). This does not alter unrelated d10/d6/d12 chains except through the feats/rules governing those dice.

rows.name: Fourtunate
rows.actors: Non-Rogue heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with d4 damage rolls
rows.effect: The actor's ordinary d4 damage dice become exploding dice. A fresh d4 explodes only on natural 4. Continuation d4s use threshold max(2, 4 - BoomShift). This is the deepest small-die explosion feat and can create frequent chains on high-DEX builds, but still obeys the universal 32-die cap.

rows.name: Quick Reload
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers; AI only if its authored weapon actually uses the shared reload authority
rows.effect: Ordinary reloads are 66% faster: ReloadTimeMultiplier = 0.34 for ordinary reloadable weapons. It does not shorten SMG overheat recovery, AR2 targeting-laser delay, Magic cooldowns, enemy authored telegraphs, or other non-reload timers.

rows.name: Field Supply
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only when they possess at least one ordinary firearm family that uses the shared ammunition-regeneration authority
rows.effect: Raises the actor's ordinary regenerative firearm AmmoRegenFloorFraction from 0.33 to 0.44. For each eligible owned family, AmmoRegenFloorRounds = ceil(MaxFamilyCapacity × 0.44). Per-round recovery is 22% faster: divide the family's existing baseline per-round interval by 1.22. The existing no-fire eligibility delay remains unchanged. Acquiring the feat grants no instant ammunition. Preserve whole-round clip-plus-reserve accounting, interruption, ownership and maximum capacity; do not create an unowned weapon or make Wand charges, consumable items or AR2 secondary ammunition regenerative.

rows.name: Disruptor
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable nonmagical damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets ArcaneDisruptionProcChance = 0.55. When an eligible physical=true, magical=false target-hit event damages a surviving target whose Arcane Shield is online, a successful proc forces exactly one post-damage Arcane Integrity save using the ordinary attacker-INT ArcaneBreakDC and defender-INT ArcaneIntegritySave formulas. This does not retag the underlying damage as magical. The physical hit remains ordinarily Feedback-eligible, and any Feedback resolution from that hit completes before this proc-created Arcane Integrity save. Magical hits do not roll this family because they already force Arcane Integrity saves automatically.

rows.name: Spellbreaker
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable nonmagical damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Disruptor and sets ArcaneDisruptionProcChance = 0.75. All shield-online eligibility, physical-damage classification, Feedback sequencing, and Arcane Integrity rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Nullifier
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable nonmagical damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Spellbreaker and sets ArcaneDisruptionProcChance = 0.95. All other Disruptor-family semantics remain unchanged. The family never rerolls or extends an already-shattered Arcane Shield timer.

rows.name: Deep Reserves
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers with regenerative firearm ammunition
rows.effect: Replaces Field Supply and raises AmmoRegenFloorFraction to 0.55. AmmoRegenFloorRounds = ceil(MaxFamilyCapacity × 0.55). Per-round recovery is 44% faster in total: divide the family's baseline interval by 1.44, without stacking lower-rank speed. Preserve the existing no-fire delay, whole-round accounting, interruption, ownership, maximum capacity and non-regenerating-resource exclusions. Acquiring the feat grants no instant ammunition.

rows.name: War Stock
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers with regenerative firearm ammunition
rows.effect: Replaces lower Field Supply ranks and raises AmmoRegenFloorFraction to 0.66. AmmoRegenFloorRounds = ceil(MaxFamilyCapacity × 0.66). Per-round recovery is 66% faster in total: divide the family's baseline interval by 1.66, without stacking lower-rank speed. Preserve the existing no-fire delay, whole-round accounting, interruption, ownership, maximum capacity and non-regenerating-resource exclusions. Acquiring the feat grants no instant ammunition. Ordinary pickups may still fill to 100% capacity, but passive regeneration stops at the feat-defined floor.

rows.name: Hair Trigger
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI whose equipped/authored ordinary firearm uses the shared attack-cadence authority
rows.effect: Single-rank, nonrepeatable Hair Trigger sets RateOfFireMultiplier=1.55: 55% faster firearm firing, with firing intervals divided by 1.55 for the revolver, pistol, shotgun, SMG and AR2. Apply the same shared multiplier to AR2 within-burst projectile spacing and the completed-burst next-trigger cycle; a burst must genuinely complete before the next trigger can begin. Preserve reloads, Magic cooldowns, SMG cooling/2-second overheat lockout, targeting-laser duration, Magnum free-projectile burst spacing and enemy telegraphs. Faster SMG firing accrues heat sooner; Heat Sink may independently suppress additions. Player-facing text: Increase firearm firing rate by 55%. Rapid Fire and Lead Storm are removed entirely, including future Hero/Soldier/AI drafts and prerequisite graphs. Existing owned or resolved historical ranks collapse to one Hair Trigger without stacking or a new award; unchosen retired offers use canonical stored-hand repair while retaining valid choices, seed and offer limit.

rows.name: Extra Round
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI actors with at least one weapon attack explicitly tagged multiFireBurst
rows.effect: BurstBonusRounds = 1. Whenever an authored attack event is already a legal multi-fire burst before feat processing, add one additional round/projectile to that burst. This feat never creates a burst from a single-fire attack and never treats exploding dice, Shotgun pellets, penetration, chained Magic projectiles, or unrelated extra-projectile procs as bursts.

rows.name: Extended Volley
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI actors with at least one weapon attack explicitly tagged multiFireBurst
rows.effect: Replaces Extra Round and sets BurstBonusRounds = 2 for eligible authored burst events.

rows.name: Full Barrage
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI actors with at least one weapon attack explicitly tagged multiFireBurst
rows.effect: Replaces Extended Volley and sets BurstBonusRounds = 3 for eligible authored burst events.

rows.name: Spring Heel
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Triples the apex height of every voluntary jump generated by the actor, including the ordinary ground jump, Wall Jump's wall-kick jump, and Cloud Step's feat-granted additional jump when those feats are owned. Under unchanged gravity, implementation scales takeoff vertical impulse to achieve 3.0x the otherwise-current jump apex rather than simply tripling vertical velocity. While the actor is legitimately airborne from voluntary movement, Spring Heel also applies AirborneHorizontalSpeedMultiplier = 1.50 to voluntary horizontal locomotion/air-control speed. This 1.50x airborne-speed effect does not amplify Wall Jump's authored lateral kick, Cloud Step's discrete directional boost, Push, knockback, scripted/base velocity, falls, ladders, stairs, conveyors, or other forced/non-voluntary motion. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative; the feat improves combat/navigation mobility but never grants permission to bypass the maze graph or locked progression.

rows.name: Wall Jump
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Grants up to four wall-assisted jumps per airborne cycle. After leaving legitimate ground, a fresh Space press first checks whether fewer than four Wall Jumps have been spent and the actor's movement hull is within WallJumpProbeDistance = 24 world units of a valid static blocking wall surface. A valid wall surface is approximately vertical, physically reachable by a short hull/trace test from the actor without crossing blocking geometry, and belongs to world/generated architecture rather than another actor, a movable physics prop, or a cosmetic/nonblocking surface. If several walls qualify, use the nearest valid surface; deterministic trace order/stable surface identity breaks an exact tie. When valid, the press consumes one of the four Wall Jumps for that airborne cycle, applies the actor's ordinary voluntary-jump vertical takeoff impulse, and adds a bounded horizontal kick directly away from the contacted wall normal. The exact lateral kick magnitude is an implementation movement-tuning value, but it must visibly clear the player hull from the wall without becoming a faster general traversal method than ordinary movement. Wall Jump costs no Magic, does not consume Cloud Step, and resets only after legitimate ground contact. A wall contact by itself never resets Wall Jump or Cloud Step, so repeated wall climbing/bouncing cannot create unlimited jumps. Input priority while airborne is WALL JUMP > CLOUD STEP > FLOAT ON: if a valid Wall Jump with a remaining use exists on a fresh Space press, it fires instead of Cloud Step; if no Wall Jump is currently eligible, Cloud Step may consume that press under its own rules; Float On is the lowest-priority hold-at-apex behavior and never intercepts a fresh Space press that can legally produce Wall Jump or Cloud Step. Spring Heel may increase Wall Jump's vertical apex under its ordinary voluntary-jump rule but does not amplify the lateral kick. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative, so Wall Jump may improve maneuvering but never authorizes container-top travel, locked-gate bypass, or movement through invalid maze geometry.

rows.name: Strafer
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Increases the actor's ordinary voluntary lateral strafe movement by 75%. StrafeSpeedMultiplier = 1.75. Apply the multiplier only to the movement component generated by left/right strafe input along the actor's local right vector; forward/backward movement remains at its otherwise-current speed. When forward/backward and strafe inputs are held together, only the lateral component receives this feat's multiplier rather than multiplying the entire combined movement vector. This modifier participates once in the ordinary locomotion-speed pipeline and may coexist with other legitimate movement-mode modifiers, but it does not alter jump impulse, airborne acceleration, ladder speed, forced Push/knockback, scripted relocation, or any non-voluntary movement.

rows.name: Little Guy
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Sets PlayerTargetScale = 0.70 while the feat is active. The third-person/world presentation and player-facing combat hurt volume scale to 70% of the ordinary character presentation, making the actor a meaningfully smaller target. The authoritative movement/collision hull, stair legality, USE reach, weapon traces, and progression interactions remain unchanged so shrinking cannot enter illegal gaps, crawl through gates, stand inside walls, or bypass canonical geometry. First-person camera/weapon presentation may be adjusted for readability but may not change authoritative reach or collision.

rows.name: Bash
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with Crowbar/melee-family access
rows.effect: The Crowbar/Long-Sword-family base damage die becomes 1d6 instead of 1d3. Every successful nonlethal hit also applies a 168-world-unit physical push through LOD.Pushback. The d6 uses the universal exploding-d6 rule. If the push is stopped by valid architecture, ordinary wall crush remains 1d3 unless another feat changes that crush.

rows.name: Walloper
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with Crowbar/melee-family access
rows.effect: The Crowbar/Long-Sword-family base damage die becomes 1d12, replacing Bash's d6 while retaining its 168-unit push. Because every d12 in LOD is a SUPER exploding d12, this melee die uses the normal fresh 8+ SUPER-d12 chain and any legal DEX BoomShift continuation effects. It does not add a d12 on top of the d6; it replaces the lower rank's base die.

rows.name: Wrecking Bar
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with Crowbar/melee-family access
rows.effect: A wall crush caused specifically by this actor's Crowbar/Long-Sword-family push uses two wall-slam dice instead of one. Without a Pusher-family feat, Wrecking Bar changes the ordinary wall-slam die count from 1d3 to 2d3; it owns die count, not die class. If Pusher, Shover, or Space Hog is also active, preserve Wrecking Bar's two-die count but raise the die class to that feat family's active wall-slam die, producing 2d8, 2d10, or 2d12 respectively rather than allowing either feat to downgrade or erase the other. The Pusher/Shover 2d8/2d10 versions are explicitly classExplosionImmune: no Rogue passive, Perfect Ten/Eight Is Enough effect, item, or other ordinary explosion-enabler may make those sealed pre-capstone wall-slam dice explode. The Space Hog 2d12 version uses the universal SUPER-d12 explosion rules for each die independently, with Rogue-class d12 thresholds if applicable. This replacement occurs once per qualifying push event and never once per sub-hit or pellet.

rows.name: Hero of Legend
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with Crowbar/Long-Sword-family access
rows.effect: Define HeroOfLegendHPThreshold = min(100, MaxHP). Whenever the actor commits a legitimate Crowbar/Long-Sword-family primary swing while CurrentHP >= HeroOfLegendHPThreshold, that swing also emits exactly one Hero of Legend pulse. The pulse is a bright laser-energy duplicate shaped to match the equipped Crowbar/Long-Sword-family weapon itself rather than a generic bolt, projected forward in the swing/aim direction, and the emission produces one distinct shrill piercing 3D sound with ordinary world attenuation. Eligibility is checked once at swing commit and is threshold-based, not exact-equality-based. If MaxHP is below 100, Hero of Legend therefore requires the actor to be at or above that lower MaxHP; if MaxHP is 100 or greater, the feat activates at CurrentHP >= 100 even when that actor's MaxHP is substantially higher. Tetris overfill and any other legitimate effect that raises CurrentHP above the threshold continue to satisfy it. Dropping below HeroOfLegendHPThreshold disables future pulses until CurrentHP returns to the threshold, while a pulse already emitted remains valid even if the actor is damaged before impact. The pulse begins immediately beyond ordinary melee reach, travels straight for at most 8 grid-cell lengths, and terminates on the first blocking world geometry or first eligible hostile hit; it cannot pass walls, closed gates, props that ordinarily block attacks, or multiple bodies. On an eligible hostile hit, resolve exactly one ranged Crowbar-family damage event using the weapon's current authored Crowbar damage die and the actor's ordinary STR PhysicalDamageMultiplier. Bash therefore upgrades the pulse from the baseline Crowbar die to d6 and Walloper upgrades it to the universal SUPER d12; all otherwise-legitimate universal explosion/continuation rules for that damage die still apply. The pulse is tagged crowbarPulse and physical for current damage/resistance authorities but is not a melee contact, does not inherit Crowbar pushback, cannot wall-crush, and does not satisfy melee-only triggers such as Momentum Fighter. It costs no ammunition and no Magic, emits at most once per committed swing, and cannot recursively generate another Hero of Legend pulse.

rows.name: Pusher
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one ordinary weapon attack capable of damaging a pushable hostile
rows.effect: Sets WeaponKnockbackProcChance = 0.55 and WeaponKnockbackProcDistance = 168 world units. After a successful nonlethal ordinary weapon hit resolves its damage against an eligible pushable hostile, make at most one deterministic Pusher-family proc roll for that resolved target-hit event. Shotgun makes one roll per damaged target per shell after pellet aggregation; each true projectile in an authored multi-projectile attack may create its own target-hit event, but individual pellets, damage dice, penetration-added dice, and Boomchain continuations never create additional proc rolls by themselves. On success, Pusher contributes exactly one independent Push-tag source to that logical target-hit event. If the hit has no other authored physical push, the proc creates a push-tagged RequestedPushDistance of 168 world units and therefore resolves as a normal single-tag Push save. If the hit already has an authored physical push, add +168 world units to that event's RequestedPushDistance before compatible multipliers and retain both independent Push-tag sources for the shared save. Thus Shotgun's inherent Push tag plus a successful Pusher-family proc produces PushTagMultiplicity = 2: there is still only one combined push and one logical PushSave event, but the defender rolls that PushSave with disadvantage under the universal duplicate save-bearing effect-tag rule. Higher Pusher-family ranks replace lower ranks and therefore remain one Pusher-family tag source rather than creating multiple copies merely from rank ownership. The completed request then resolves through the shared STR-based push save before LOD.Pushback collision/movement resolution. On failure, a pre-existing push still resolves normally. Pusher-family proc generation also uses a shared per-attacker/per-target success cooldown: PusherProcTargetCooldownSeconds = 0.50. While that cooldown is active for the same attacker-target pair, later hits make no Pusher-family proc roll, although any authored push on those hits still resolves normally. A successful Pusher-family proc starts the 0.50-second cooldown; a failed eligible roll does not. Different targets track cooldown independently. Separately and regardless of whether the proc succeeded, this actor's ordinary physical-push wall-slam/wall-crush base die becomes 1d8 instead of the shared 1d3. Pusher-family d8 wall-slam dice are tagged classExplosionImmune=true. They are deliberately non-exploding for every class and cannot be made explosive by Rogue mastery, Eight Is Enough, equipment, or another ordinary explosion-enabler; unlocking explosion inside this family is reserved for Space Hog. The knockback proc is a utility proc, not a damage die, and is not Luck-Ring eligible unless a later rule explicitly says otherwise.

rows.name: Shover
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one ordinary weapon attack capable of damaging a pushable hostile
rows.effect: Replaces Pusher and sets WeaponKnockbackProcChance = 0.75 while retaining WeaponKnockbackProcDistance = 168 world units. On a successful proc, an otherwise non-pushing weapon hit gains a push-tagged RequestedPushDistance of 168 world units and an already-pushing hit gains +168 units to its RequestedPushDistance; the completed request then resolves through the shared STR-based push save before physical displacement. The actor's ordinary physical-push wall-slam/wall-crush base die becomes 1d10. Shover-family d10 wall-slam dice are tagged classExplosionImmune=true. They remain non-exploding for every class and cannot be made explosive by Rogue mastery, Perfect Ten, equipment, or another ordinary explosion-enabler. Shover inherits PusherProcTargetCooldownSeconds = 0.50 and all per-attacker/per-target cooldown semantics. All Pusher targeting, aggregation, collision, one-proc-per-target-hit, and non-Luck-Ring rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Space Hog
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one ordinary weapon attack capable of damaging a pushable hostile
rows.effect: Replaces Shover and sets WeaponKnockbackProcChance = 0.95 while retaining WeaponKnockbackProcDistance = 168 world units. On a successful proc, an otherwise non-pushing weapon hit gains a push-tagged RequestedPushDistance of 168 world units and an already-pushing hit gains +168 units to its RequestedPushDistance; the completed request then resolves through the shared STR-based push save before physical displacement. The actor's ordinary physical-push wall-slam/wall-crush base die becomes 1d12. Space Hog removes the lower ranks' classExplosionImmune seal. Because every d12 in LOD is a SUPER exploding d12, Space Hog is the first and only rank in this family whose wall-slam die explodes: a fresh wall-slam d12 begins at the universal 8+ threshold and subsequent continuation dice use the ordinary descending SUPER-d12 rule plus any legal DEX BoomShift assistance. Higher Pusher-family ranks replace, rather than stack with, the lower rank's proc chance and wall-slam die. Space Hog inherits PusherProcTargetCooldownSeconds = 0.50. A single resolved push can still cause at most one wall crush.

rows.name: Steamroller
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one authored push-capable attack or effect
rows.effect: Whenever a push-tagged event credited to this actor reaches the shared STR push save, a successful PushSave applies 50% of SizeAdjustedPushDistance instead of the ordinary 0%; a failed PushSave still applies 100%. Steamroller does not create push where none exists, does not alter PushDC or PushSave, does not grant extra saves, and never bypasses PushImmune. Any resulting nonzero displacement continues through ordinary defender-side post-save multipliers, LOD.Pushback collision handling, and wall-slam/wall-crush rules.

rows.name: Bloodletter
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets BleedProcChance = 0.55 under the shared status-proc feat-family rules. On an eligible target-hit event, a successful proc creates exactly one Bleeding application attempt. Bloodletter is STR-governed for feat qualification, but Bleeding remains a canonical CON-resisted condition: the attacker's CON sets BleedDC and the defender's CON sets BleedSave. A successful save prevents Bleeding. If the authored attack already guarantees a Bleeding application attempt, skip the redundant Bloodletter-family proc roll.

rows.name: Deep Wounds
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Bloodletter and sets BleedProcChance = 0.75. All shared target-hit aggregation, CON-based BleedDC/BleedSave, Bleeding tick/recovery, and non-stacking rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Exsanguinator
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Deep Wounds and sets BleedProcChance = 0.95. All other Bloodletter-family semantics remain unchanged; higher ranks replace rather than stack with lower ranks, and BleedTickDamage can never itself roll Bloodletter or another offensive status-proc family.

rows.name: Long Reach
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes/human Soldiers with melee-family access
rows.effect: Ordinary melee-family reach is multiplied by 1.25, after which the existing geometry trace remains authoritative. This cannot strike through walls, gates, floors, or other blocking architecture.

rows.name: Blast-Proof
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Once every 2.0 seconds per defender, when an incoming damage die would legitimately create a continuation die because its kept result met that die chain's current explosion threshold, Blast-Proof suppresses that one explosion continuation. The triggering die still contributes its full resolved damage value; only the continuation die that would have been created is omitted. The 2.0-second cooldown begins when a continuation is actually suppressed. While the cooldown is active, later explosion events resolve normally. Blast-Proof applies to any incoming actor-owned damage die that can generate an explosion continuation, including universal d6/SUPER-d12 chains, feat-enabled exploding d4/d8/d10 damage dice, and future exploding Magic damage dice. It does not trigger on non-damage count dice such as Shotgun pellet-count rolls, health-generation dice, loot/progression/random utility rolls, or the defender's own outgoing damage rolls. If one attack contains several independent exploding damage dice, only the first qualifying continuation encountered in authoritative resolution order is suppressed while Blast-Proof is ready. It may suppress either an initiating explosion or a later continuation explosion; in either case that specific chain ends at the suppressed die because no next die is created. The combat-roll feed records BLAST-PROOF when a continuation is prevented.

rows.name: Big Guy
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Sets PlayerTargetScale to 1.30. Third-person/world presentation and combat hurt volume become 130% size while the authoritative movement/collision hull remains unchanged. Melee reach is multiplied by 1.15 and actor-authored physical push dealt is multiplied by 1.20. The larger hurt volume is the balancing drawback. Big Guy and Little Guy are mutually exclusive.

rows.name: Not Yet
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with a personal-life ledger
rows.effect: Adds NotYetLifeCapBonus = +1 to the owner's current personal-life cap. The ordinary baseline personal-life cap is 4, so a Hero with no other cap modifiers can hold up to 5 lives while owning Not Yet. This is an additive cap modifier: future authored effects that raise the personal-life cap may stack with Not Yet rather than being overwritten by it. Acquiring Not Yet raises only the maximum; it does not immediately grant, restore, or refill a personal life. Extra-life pickups and overflow-revival logic use the Hero's resulting current cap.

rows.name: Russian Asset
rows.actors: Player-controlled cooperative heroes with Tetris access
rows.effect: Primary ability: while alive in ordinary active-dungeon play, enter LEFT → RIGHT → UP → DOWN using keyboard arrows or controller/Steam Input D-pad. This feat-specific sequence may accept D-pad input independently of ordinary Special Move restrictions. A successful opening requires at least 15 Magic and spends exactly 15 once; insufficient Magic spends nothing. Live Tetris has no continuing Magic drain or time limit and may be voluntarily closed with F; a finished board may restart within the same paid live session. The world does not pause: enemies remain active and may attack or kill the player, with no invulnerability, aggro suppression or safety grant. Live line clears heal immediately: single +20, double +60, triple +100, quad +160 HP, capped at ordinary MaxHP; excess is discarded and cannot bank or extend temporary overfill. Death, disconnect, actor/role/run/dungeon replacement, reset and other authoritative lifecycle closure invalidate the session and stale inputs. Secondary benefits remain: doubles all temporary HP overfill earned from qualifying death/victory Tetris line-clear rewards: TetrisOverfillMultiplier = 2.0, so the baseline single/double/triple/quad rewards become +20/+60/+100/+160 HP and all accumulated qualifying Tetris reward is doubled before being applied. This reward multiplier applies to both death Tetris and post-rescue/victory Tetris. Separately, only for death Tetris, DeathTetrisMaxSeconds increases from the normally hidden 60-second hard cap to 120 seconds. Russian Asset does not change the mandatory 20-second death/respawn lockout, does not delay the moment F becomes available to respawn, does not require the player to remain dead for 120 seconds, and does not extend post-rescue/victory Tetris beyond its ordinary 20-second duration. Pressing F at any eligible time after the 20-second minimum still immediately finalizes the current death-Tetris score and respawns normally.

rows.name: Heat Sink
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers who possess/use the SMG
rows.effect: Sets SMGHeatSuppressionChance = 0.66 and SMGOverheatThreshold = 8 heat. On every successfully fired SMG round, before that round adds its normal one shot-equivalent of heat, the server makes one deterministic heat-suppression roll from the dedicated SMG-heat substream. Heat Sink heat-suppression rolls are not Luck-Ring eligible and cannot be rerolled or advantaged unless a later feat explicitly says otherwise. On success, that round adds 0 heat; on failure, it adds the ordinary +1 heat. The SMG overheats when accumulated heat reaches 8 rather than the baseline 6. Damage, ammunition consumption, fire rate, sub-threshold cooling, visual/audio heat stages, and the fixed 2.0-second overheat lockout are unchanged.

rows.name: Snap Targeting
rows.actors: Player-controlled actors using the AR2
rows.effect: The player AR2's pre-burst targeting-laser delay is multiplied by 0.80, never below a 0.50-second absolute readability floor. The weapon still requires the laser tell before every three-round burst.

rows.name: Deadeye
rows.actors: Player-controlled actors using the .357 Magnum
rows.effect: Magnum Aim State requires 0.35 seconds of perfect stillness instead of 0.50 seconds. Movement, jump input, aim movement, weapon switching, death, and firing cancel/consume the state exactly as normal.

rows.name: Mana Barrier
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Sets ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.15. This feat family is unavailable to Wizard-class actors; it is the INT-gated HP→Magic diversion path for eligible non-Wizards. For an eligible non-Wizard with Mana Barrier, Mana Barrier grants ArcaneShieldCapability and HPToMagicDiversionFraction = ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.15 while Arcane Shield is online; while shattered, effective HPToMagicDiversionFraction = 0 until the shared 5d6! shatter timer clears. After an incoming damage event has completed all ordinary damage resolution, including attack dice/Boomchains, weakness/resistance/immunity handling, CON DamageResistancePerDie, and other authored mitigation or amplification, but immediately before HP is removed, define ResolvedHPDamage as the HP damage that would otherwise be applied; it may be fractional. DesiredHPDiversion = ResolvedHPDamage × HPToMagicDiversionFraction. ActualHPDiversion = min(DesiredHPDiversion, CurrentMagic). MagicSpent = ActualHPDiversion and FinalHPDamage = ResolvedHPDamage - ActualHPDiversion. Fractional HP diversion and fractional Magic damage are legal. Magic cannot fall below 0. This diversion authority applies to ordinary damage events from actors or the environment, including damage to temporary Tetris overfill, but not direct kill commands, non-damage death states, or effects explicitly tagged ignoreManaBarrier. HP-to-Magic diversion loss is classified as Magic damage, not voluntary Magic spending, so spend/cast triggers do not fire merely because the barrier absorbed damage. If the barrier reduces Magic to 0, normal zero-Magic consequences still occur, including forced minimap closure; ordinary regeneration rules then govern recovery.

rows.name: Arcane Aegis
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Replaces Mana Barrier and sets ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.30. This feat remains unavailable to Wizard-class actors. For eligible non-Wizards, HPToMagicDiversionFraction = 0.30. The same post-mitigation continuous calculation and 1 Magic per 1 prevented HP exchange apply; fractional HP diversion and fractional Magic damage are legal, diversion is limited by CurrentMagic, and any unpayable remainder is taken as HP damage normally.

rows.name: Mystic Bastion
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Replaces lower Mana Barrier ranks and sets ManaBarrierFeatDiversionFraction = 0.45. This feat remains unavailable to Wizard-class actors. For eligible non-Wizards, HPToMagicDiversionFraction = 0.45. It never increases Magic capacity above 100, explicitly permits fractional HP prevention and fractional Magic damage, never prevents non-damage death, and remains constrained by the actor's CurrentMagic.

rows.name: Mana Spring
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Magic regenerates 22% faster whenever ordinary regeneration is legally permitted: multiply the otherwise resolved INT-scaled passive regeneration rate, including existing compatible modifiers, by 1.22 exactly once. No zero-Magic trigger, duration, cooldown or activation cost. Minimap and every other authored regeneration suppression remain absolute. Capacity stays 100; direct Magic refunds, costs and drains are unchanged.

rows.name: Cloud Step
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Grants exactly one additional voluntary jump per airborne cycle. After leaving authoritative ground, a fresh Space press while airborne may consume 5 Magic to perform one additional jump; if fewer than 5 Magic is available, no Cloud Step occurs and no partial cost is paid. The additional jump uses ordinary jump strength unless another compatible movement feat modifies voluntary jump height; Spring Heel therefore triples both the ground jump and Cloud Step jump when both are owned. When Wall Jump is also owned, a fresh airborne Space press that has a valid unused Wall Jump resolves Wall Jump first and leaves Cloud Step unused; once the actor is no longer eligible for that wall jump, a later fresh Space press may still consume Cloud Step normally. Cloud Step and Wall Jump are separate once-per-airborne-cycle resources and may therefore both occur before the next legitimate ground contact. Cloud Step resets only after legitimate ground contact and cannot create repeated air jumps from wall contact, props, Push, or scripted movement. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative.

rows.name: Float On
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Once per airborne cycle, the actor may hold Space at the apex of an eligible jump to enter a controllable float for up to 6.0 seconds. Float On spends Magic continuously at 1 Magic per second, so using the complete 6.0-second duration costs exactly 6 Magic; partial use costs only the proportional amount actually floated. The float ends immediately when Space is released, the 6.0-second cap is reached, available Magic is exhausted, or legitimate ground contact occurs. Floating suppresses ordinary downward acceleration enough to maintain the intended brief Princess-Peach-style hang time but does not create upward flight; ordinary horizontal air control remains available. Once Float On has been started or exhausted during an airborne cycle, it cannot be started again until legitimate ground contact resets it. Float On is always the lowest-priority Space behavior. A fresh airborne Space press that can legally trigger Wall Jump or Cloud Step resolves that discrete jump instead of starting Float. If Cloud Step is owned and still unused, Float On remains ineligible at an earlier apex; it may activate only after Cloud Step has actually been performed. When Wall Jump is also owned, Wall Jump may occur before or after Cloud Step according to wall proximity, and a later eligible apex may still start Float; merely owning an unused Wall Jump does not suppress Float when no valid wall is currently within WallJumpProbeDistance. This supports the canonical sequence ground jump -> Wall Jump when near a wall -> Cloud Step after moving clear -> hold Space at the later apex for Float, while also supporting ground jump -> Cloud Step -> Wall Jump -> Float if the actor reaches a wall later in the same airborne cycle. Without Cloud Step, Float On may activate at the apex of the ordinary ground jump or, if a Wall Jump was used afterward, at the later Wall Jump apex. Canonical anti-top, gate, ceiling, and progression blockers remain authoritative.

rows.name: Quantum Mathematics
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible active attack-tagged Magic activation
rows.effect: Reduces the Magic cost of eligible offensive Magic activated through RMB or the equivalent rebindable active-Magic action by 22%. QuantumCostMultiplier = 0.78. EligibleOffensiveMagicBaseCost is the ordinary resolved Magic cost that would otherwise be spent for that damaging/attack-tagged activation after its authored Form/Content combination and other ordinary base-cost construction but before this feat-family reduction. FinalOffensiveMagicCost = max(1, ceil(EligibleOffensiveMagicBaseCost × QuantumCostMultiplier)). This feat affects only Magic actually spent to initiate eligible offensive attack Magic; it does not change Magic regeneration, Max Magic, Magic damage, dice, Boom rules, status chances, cooldowns, Arcane Shield diversion, Feedback, the minimap, Haste, Polymorph, GPS, passive/supplemental Magic effects, or any other utility/non-attack Magic cost. Within this feat family, only the highest owned rank applies.

rows.name: Quantum Mechanics
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible active attack-tagged Magic activation
rows.effect: Replaces Quantum Mathematics' 22% reduction with a 44% reduction to eligible offensive RMB/equivalent active-Magic costs. QuantumCostMultiplier = 0.56 and FinalOffensiveMagicCost = max(1, ceil(EligibleOffensiveMagicBaseCost × 0.56)). All eligibility, exclusions, rounding, and non-stacking rules from Quantum Mathematics remain authoritative.

rows.name: Quantum Mastery
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, and AI with at least one eligible active attack-tagged Magic activation
rows.effect: Replaces Quantum Mechanics' 44% reduction with a 66% reduction to eligible offensive RMB/equivalent active-Magic costs. QuantumCostMultiplier = 0.34 and FinalOffensiveMagicCost = max(1, ceil(EligibleOffensiveMagicBaseCost × 0.34)). All eligibility, exclusions, rounding, and non-stacking rules from Quantum Mathematics remain authoritative.

rows.name: Middle Manager
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with the Summon Form unlocked
rows.effect: Raises that Hero's caster-specific MaxActiveSummons from the default 1 to 2. This is a cap replacement, not an additive +1 stack. It changes only the number of that caster's own allied Seeker summons that may coexist; it does not alter Summon duration, Magic cost, placement range, Seeker attack behavior, inherited SummonMagicPayload, Content, damage, or AI behavior. If the caster is already at the cap, another Summon cast is illegal and spends no Magic rather than replacing an existing summon.

rows.name: Taskmaster
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with the Summon Form unlocked
rows.effect: Raises that Hero's caster-specific MaxActiveSummons to 3, replacing the Middle Manager cap rather than stacking with it. All Summon cost, duration, placement, payload inheritance, Content, damage, AI, and lifecycle rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Overlord
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with the Summon Form unlocked
rows.effect: Raises that Hero's caster-specific MaxActiveSummons to 4, replacing the Taskmaster cap rather than stacking with it. Four is the authored maximum unless a future explicit rule changes it. All other Summon rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Aftershock
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with at least one unlocked non-Summon Magic Form
rows.effect: Each successful committed cast of BLAST, BEAM, BOMB, MISSILE, or BOLT schedules exactly one phantom echo 0.50 seconds later at no additional Magic cost. The server snapshots the original cast's launch origin, authoritative maze cell where applicable, launch orientation or initial vector, Form identity, selected Content damage type, and the caster-side Magic damage state needed to reproduce that attack. The echo originates from that exact captured launch point and initial direction, never from the caster's position 0.50 seconds later. It uses the original Form's geometry, collision rules, target budget, delivery behavior, selected Content damage type, WIS MagicPowerMultiplier, elemental damage resolution, Boom authority, and all other otherwise-applicable caster-side Magic damage modifiers, but reduces only the Form's authored base damage-die count according to AftershockDiceCount = max(1, floor(OriginalFormBaseDamageDiceCount / 2)). With the current Form catalog this yields Blast 1d6, Beam 1d6, Bomb 1d6, Missile 1d6, and Bolt 2d6 before ordinary scaling and Boom resolution. The echo is damage-only and carries no Content rider, status, control, Push, or other non-damage rider: Earth creates no Push; Fire no Immolated; Dark no Poisoned; Ice no Held; Light no Muted; Electric no Morale rider. Current target-side weakness, resistance, immunity, blockers, collision, and other ordinary Magic interactions are resolved when the phantom attack actually launches or lands. Aftershock never triggers from SUMMON, summoned-Seeker proxy attacks, another Aftershock echo, passive or scripted Magic, or a failed or cancelled cast, and an echo cannot recursively schedule another echo. A committed original cast still produces its scheduled echo if the caster moves afterward; only invalid session/level cleanup or cancellation before original cast commitment removes the pending echo. The phantom is a real second Form attack against then-current world state, not delayed guaranteed damage to the original targets. Its visual presentation reuses the Form effect at AftershockVisualAlpha = 0.50 × OriginalVisualAlpha and deterministically generates the complementary opposite color by rotating the original effect hue 180 degrees while preserving saturation and lightness/value as closely as renderer constraints allow; achromatic originals use a deterministic high-contrast complementary fallback. For steerable Missile, the echo begins from the captured original launch transform and thereafter retains ordinary Missile steering behavior; the other eligible Forms use their corresponding captured-origin semantics.

rows.name: World Walker
rows.actors: Player-controlled Heroes and human Soldiers with ordinary minimap access
rows.effect: While this actor's personal minimap is actually open, MapOpenMovementMultiplier = 1.25. Apply this to the actor's ordinary voluntary locomotion speed after walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. The bonus begins only after the map is successfully opened and ends immediately when it closes for any reason. It does not alter jump velocity, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, Push/knockback, falling, projectile motion, or forced movement. If Haste is owned, first resolve the ordinary map-modified walking or sprinting speed and then apply HasteMovementMultiplier = 1.33; this composes through the same locomotion pipeline rather than creating a parallel speed algorithm. Haste itself consumes no Magic. Within this feat family, only the highest owned rank applies. The feat provides no benefit when lod_mapless or another authoritative state prevents the minimap from opening.

rows.name: Globetrotter
rows.actors: Player-controlled Heroes and human Soldiers with ordinary minimap access
rows.effect: Replaces World Walker's 25% map-open movement bonus with MapOpenMovementMultiplier = 1.50. All activation, forced-close, locomotion, Haste composition, mapless, and non-stacking rules from World Walker remain authoritative.

rows.name: Mind Strider
rows.actors: Player-controlled Heroes and human Soldiers with ordinary minimap access
rows.effect: Replaces Globetrotter's 50% map-open movement bonus with MapOpenMovementMultiplier = 1.75. All activation, forced-close, locomotion, Haste composition, mapless, and non-stacking rules from World Walker remain authoritative.

rows.name: Grand Unified Theory
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with at least one eligible unowned Magic Form
rows.effect: Immediately grants two distinct currently-unowned Magic Forms from the existing class-eligible canonical Form catalog. If exactly one remains, grant that one; with none remaining, the feat is ineligible and must not be offered. Each grant is selected deterministically without replacement using the dedicated grand_unified_theory RNG substream; the player does not choose it, and acquisition never rerolls because I is opened, closed, or revisited. The Form persists for that campaign exactly like a scheduled class-progression Form grant. Grand Unified Theory composes with the synchronized class milestone chart rather than replacing it: a Wizard who would normally own four Forms by Level 10 may reach six, while a Rogue or Fighter who would normally own two may reach four, limited by the class-eligible catalog actually remaining. If this feat is acquired before a later scheduled Form grant, that later grant selects another still-unowned Form when available; no duplicate or wasted Form is generated until the class-eligible catalog is exhausted. A Hero who already owns every class-eligible Form is ineligible for this feat and it must not be offered as a dead choice. Grand Unified Theory grants no Content, does not alter Form damage, Magic costs, WIS/Astral spatial scaling, Boom rules, or spell-selection limits, and does not grant Wizard-only class passives.

rows.name: Extracurricular Activity
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with fewer than all six canonical Contents unlocked
rows.effect: Immediately grants two distinct currently-unowned Contents from the canonical six-Content catalog. If exactly one remains, grant that one; with none remaining, the feat is ineligible and must not be offered. Each grant is selected deterministically without replacement using the dedicated extracurricular_activity RNG substream; the player does not choose it, and acquisition never rerolls because I is opened, closed, or revisited. The Content persists for that campaign exactly like a scheduled class-progression Content grant and may be attached to any owned compatible Magic Form through the ordinary shared Form/Content spellcasting authority. Extracurricular Activity composes with the synchronized Level-1/4/8/14 Wizard Content track and existing non-Wizard track rather than replacing it: a Wizard who would normally own four Contents by Level 14 may reach six, while a Rogue or Fighter who would normally own one may reach three, limited by the remaining catalog. If this feat is acquired before a later scheduled Content grant, that later grant selects another still-unowned Content when available; no duplicate or wasted Content is generated until the six-Content catalog is exhausted. A Hero who already owns all six Contents is ineligible for this feat and it must not be offered as a dead choice. Extracurricular Activity grants no Magic Form, does not alter Form or Content damage, Magic costs, WIS/Astral spatial scaling, Boom rules, status rider strength, or spell-selection limits, and does not grant Wizard-only class passives.

rows.name: Polymorph
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Adds a dedicated rebindable Polymorph action whose default keyboard binding is J. Activation is legal only while alive, player-controlled, not already polymorphed, and CurrentMagic = 100. Pressing the Polymorph action consumes the entire Magic pool immediately, sets CurrentMagic = 0, and transforms the actor into a chicken for PolymorphDurationSeconds = 4d6! seconds. Each of the four duration d6 chains uses the universal fixed natural-6 recursive explosion rule; these are timing dice rather than damage dice and therefore do not inherit Rogue damage-die mastery, DEX BoomShift, Wizard magical Boom rules, weapon-specific thresholds, or other damage-die modifiers. Minimum duration is 4 seconds, there is no fixed maximum, and expected duration is 16.8 seconds. Polymorph cannot be cancelled voluntarily once begun. While in chicken form, the actor is removed from ordinary hostile AI target-candidate selection and any AI target lock that exists only because that actor was a hostile target is cleared immediately; this is temporary target suppression, not a faction change, charm, invulnerability, or deletion from combat. AI may not deliberately reacquire or aim a new hostile attack at the chicken until the form ends. Attacks/projectiles already validly committed before transformation may finish resolving, and the chicken remains fully vulnerable to incidental line-of-fire hits, penetration, explosions, cones, persistent hazards, environmental damage, status damage, Reckless-friendly-fire geometry, and any other damage source that reaches it without requiring a new hostile target selection. Chicken form is a disengagement utility state: the actor cannot initiate weapon fire, melee attacks, damaging Magic, active spellcasting, or other attack-tagged actions while transformed. Tapping Space while airborne performs a chicken flap that adds another ordinary upward jump impulse; there is no per-airborne-cycle flap count while Polymorph remains active, so repeated taps create the intended comic chicken flight. Canonical ceilings, anti-container-top blockers, locked gates, progression barriers, map bounds, and other topology protections remain authoritative, so repeated flapping can aid escape and vertical maneuvering but can never fly over or through forbidden progression geometry. The world model becomes a readable chicken presentation and emits intermittent spatialized chicken clucks/boks during the transformation; audiovisual presentation must not obscure combat information. When PolymorphDurationSeconds expires, the actor automatically returns to their ordinary character form and normal hostile-target eligibility. Magic regeneration remains suppressed for PolymorphPostRecoveryDelaySeconds = 5.0 after reversion; after that delay, ordinary INT-scaled Magic regeneration rules resume. Because a new Polymorph requires CurrentMagic = 100 again, the full-pool requirement plus forced zeroing and post-form regeneration delay provide the feat's effective cooldown without a second independent cooldown timer.

rows.name: W,A,S,Deborah
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: While the actor is voluntarily moving with backward movement input, BackpedalMovementMultiplier = 1.25. Backpedaling is true whenever the actor has nonzero voluntary horizontal movement input and their signed forward/back movement input is negative relative to their current facing; holding S alone or together with lateral movement therefore qualifies, while pure strafing, forward movement, knockback, Push, sliding, falling, and other forced movement do not. Apply BackpedalMovementMultiplier to the actor's resolved voluntary locomotion speed after ordinary walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. It does not replace or disable normal sprint. If Haste is owned, its passive 1.33 multiplier applies normally to the already backpedal-modified legal locomotion speed, so the two feats compose multiplicatively rather than through a separate movement authority. The feat changes no forward-only movement, pure lateral movement, jump velocity, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, projectile motion, or forced movement.

rows.name: Haste
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Passively increases ordinary voluntary movement speed by 33%: HasteMovementMultiplier = 1.33. Apply it once to the actor's resolved voluntary horizontal locomotion after ordinary walk/run/sprint mode, DEX movement scaling, MapOpenMovementMultiplier when applicable, and other compatible ordinary movement modifiers. Haste has no activation input, Magic cost, drain, cooldown, or regeneration suppression. It never replaces, consumes, disables, or changes access to ordinary sprint. Haste changes no jump velocity, airborne acceleration, Wall Jump, Cloud Step, Float On, Push/knockback, falling, projectile motion, scripted relocation, or other forced/non-voluntary movement.

rows.name: Feedback Loop
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Whenever the owner actually loses HP to a resolved damage event, snapshot the real HP loss after ordinary mitigation/diversion and canonical aggregation. Roll one sealed non-exploding 1d4-second delay through the feat-specific timing RNG. On expiration, refund Magic equal to 50% of that actual HP loss, preserving fractions and capping CurrentMagic at 100. Zero HP loss produces no refund. Each canonical event owns exactly one delayed refund; pellets, internal sub-hits and damage dice cannot duplicate it. Validate originating actor identity/state/incarnation/life, run/dungeon and module generation at payout; death, disconnect, reset, replacement and hot reload invalidate stale payouts. This has no offensive-Magic continuation-die behavior.

rows.name: Arc Recovery
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, Magic-using AI
rows.effect: Whenever the owner deals Magic-tagged actual HP damage, snapshot the real health lost by that resolved target-damage event after mitigation/diversion and canonical aggregation. Roll one sealed non-exploding 1d4-second delay through isolated feat timing RNG. On expiration, refund Magic equal to 50% of the actual HP damage dealt; preserve fractions and cap CurrentMagic at 100. Misses, immunity, zero HP loss and nonmagical damage create no refund. Resolve once per canonical damaged target, never per die/pellet/internal sub-hit. Validate originating actor identity/state/incarnation/life, run/dungeon and module generation at payout; stale damage cannot fund a later life or run. There is no kill requirement or former two-second kill cooldown.

rows.name: Cartographer
rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers with minimap access
rows.effect: Adds +8 to BreadcrumbCells after the normal WIS formula. The additional route length follows the same canonical current-objective route and player-facing navigation authority as the ordinary breadcrumb. Current-floor and canonical current-objective routing restrictions remain absolute.

rows.name: Hushing
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets MuteProcChance = 0.55. On an eligible target-hit event under the common status-proc rules, a successful proc creates one mute-tagged application attempt using the ordinary attacker-WIS MagicDC and defender-WIS MagicSave formulas. Failure applies canonical Muted; success prevents it.

rows.name: Silencing
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Hushing and sets MuteProcChance = 0.75. All common status-proc aggregation, WIS-save, Muted duration, passive-Magic preservation, and non-stacking rules remain unchanged.

rows.name: Dead Air
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Silencing and sets MuteProcChance = 0.95. All other Hushing-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend Muted under its existing later-expiration rule.

rows.name: Snaring
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets HeldProcChance = 0.55 under the shared status-proc feat-family rules. On a successful proc, the target makes exactly one ordinary WIS MagicSave against the attacker's WIS-based MagicDC; failure applies canonical Held. This creates a Held attempt only and never bypasses the defender's Wisdom.

rows.name: Binding
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Snaring and sets HeldProcChance = 0.75. All other Snaring-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend Held under its existing later-expiration rule.

rows.name: Entrapping
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Binding and sets HeldProcChance = 0.95. All other Snaring-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend Held under its existing later-expiration rule.

rows.name: Agitating
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Sets RecklessProcChance = 0.55 under the shared status-proc feat-family rules. On a successful proc, the target makes exactly one ordinary WIS MagicSave against the attacker's WIS-based MagicDC; failure applies canonical Reckless. This creates a Reckless attempt only and never bypasses the defender's Wisdom.

rows.name: Unhinging
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Agitating and sets RecklessProcChance = 0.75. All other Agitating-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend Reckless under its existing later-expiration rule.

rows.name: Maddening
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI with at least one eligible attributable damaging attack
rows.effect: Replaces Unhinging and sets RecklessProcChance = 0.95. All other Agitating-family semantics remain unchanged; repeated failed applications may only extend Reckless under its existing later-expiration rule.

rows.name: Frugal Cartography
rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers with minimap access
rows.effect: After the normal WIS UtilityMagicCostMultiplier is calculated, minimap drain is multiplied by an additional 0.75, with final MapDrainPerSecond never lower than 3.0 Magic/second. Magic regeneration remains completely disabled while the map is open. Frugal Cartography modifies minimap drain only; passive Haste consumes no Magic and is unaffected by this feat.

rows.name: True Faith
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Grants MagicalDamageReduction = max(0, WIS_MOD). Whenever this actor receives an incoming damage event tagged magical=true from any source, reduce that event's aggregated magical damage by MagicalDamageReduction after ordinary damage dice/Boom resolution, CON DamageResistancePerDie, source-side scaling, and elemental/identity modifiers, but before Arcane Shield HP-to-Magic diversion, lethal intercepts, and final HP loss. Apply True Faith exactly once per resolved damage event, never once per die, pellet, Boom continuation, or internal sub-hit, and never reduce damage below 0. Physical-only events with magical=false receive no reduction. If an unusual event is tagged both physical=true and magical=true, it qualifies because it is still an explicitly magical damage source. True Faith does not alter MagicSave, Arcane Integrity, elemental resistance/weakness, status saves, Magic cost, or any non-damage effect.

rows.name: Mind Over Matter
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: While this feat is ready, the first incoming damage event tagged physical=true automatically receives PhysicalDamageReduction = max(0, WIS_MOD), applied once to the event's aggregated physical damage after ordinary damage dice/Boom resolution, CON DamageResistancePerDie, source-side scaling, and elemental/identity modifiers, but before Arcane Shield HP-to-Magic diversion, lethal intercepts, and final HP loss. Never reduce damage below 0. After an eligible physical event consumes the ready state, set MindOverMatterCooldownSeconds = 3.0 seconds and do not apply Mind Over Matter again until that fixed cooldown expires. No timing dice are rolled or reported. When the cooldown expires, Mind Over Matter becomes ready again. Magical-only events with physical=false do not consume the ready state. A mixed physical=true/magical=true event may receive True Faith's magical reduction and, when Mind Over Matter is ready, Mind Over Matter's physical reduction on the same resolved event; each applies once and final damage is clamped at 0. Mind Over Matter does not alter Push, wall-slam damage, hit-stun, status saves, MagicSave, or any non-damage physical effect.

rows.name: GPS
rows.actors: Player-controlled Heroes only
rows.effect: Adds a private old-school synthetic GPS navigation assist with a dedicated rebindable toggle whose default keyboard binding is G. GPS starts enabled immediately when the feat is acquired. Acquisition displays a concise tooltip/system notice: GPS ENABLED — If it gets annoying, press G to turn it off. Press G again to turn it back on. Pressing the GPS action toggles the feature without spending Magic; every toggle plays a short electronic switch/chime and produces the ordinary bounded on-screen system notice GPS ON or GPS OFF. While enabled, GPS speaks automatically after 1 second standing still with no nearby living enemies. Aim/facing may change while stationary. Repeat while still safe and stationary, with a 4-second silence after the previous phrase finishes; there is no random idle die or one-bark limit. Nearby means the same floor within 2 cells using max(abs(dx), abs(dy)), including enemies behind walls and human Soldiers. Movement, nearby enemies, combat, death/spectating, staging or cutscenes reset the idle trigger and cancel pending speech. Keep one private voice channel, cancel stale asynchronous callbacks, and resolve the current canonical route afresh for each phrase. When triggered, GPS reads only the authoritative canonical route from the Hero's current cell to the currently active progression objective and emits one short 2000s/early-2010s-style direction assembled from a small fixed synthetic/concatenative voice bank. Supported phrase families include TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, TURN AROUND, CONTINUE FORWARD, IN N SQUARES TURN LEFT/RIGHT, IN N SQUARES TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, TAKE THE STAIRS UP/DOWN, and YOU HAVE ARRIVED AT YOUR DESTINATION. N is derived from the contiguous legal route segment to the next turn, stair transition, or objective rather than guessed. GPS never invents a shortcut, predicts future progression stages, reveals enemies or loot, or performs a second pathfinding authority: it consumes the same canonical current-objective route used by ordinary navigation/breadcrumb logic. GPS is supplemental information and remains available even when lod_mapless 1 removes the visual minimap; it does not itself reveal a map or persistent route display. Active combat, death/spectating, staging, cutscenes, and other states where a navigation bark would be intrusive suspend the idle trigger. GPS has no Magic cost and does not alter Magic regeneration, BreadcrumbCells, movement, combat statistics, rewards, or objective logic.

rows.name: Astral Reach
rows.actors: Cooperative Heroes with at least one Magic Form unlocked
rows.effect: Adds AstralReachBonusCells = 2 to the shared Magic Form spatial-scaling authority. This flat +2-cell bonus layers on top of the caster's ordinary MagicSpatialBonusCells = max(1, WIS_MOD); it does not replace Wisdom scaling or create a second range algorithm. The +2 applies only to each Form dimension already marked Wisdom-scaled: Blast gains +2 cells of graph reach; Beam gains +2 cells of linear reach; Bomb keeps fixed throw range but gains +2 cells of explosion radius; Missile gains +2 cells of guided-flight range and +2 cells of explosion radius; Bolt gains +2 cells of projectile reach. Future Magic Forms inherit the same semantic rule automatically: Astral Reach adds +2 cells to each spatial dimension the core Wisdom authority marks scalable and does nothing to dimensions the Form keeps static. Existing geometry, obstruction, target-once, penetration, and attack-work rules remain unchanged. Astral Reach changes no damage dice, Magic cost, Boom rules, Content surcharge/riders, Push, status behavior, projectile speed, steering responsiveness, minimap range, BreadcrumbCells, GPS, Force Shout, or any non-Form system.

rows.name: Spatial Awareness
rows.actors: Player-controlled heroes and human Soldiers only
rows.effect: Warns about visible hostile monsters behind you and directly to either side. RearRangeCells = max(1, WIS_MOD), without Astral Reach. Quantize horizontal facing to the nearest cardinal maze direction. The rear footprint remains three cells wide for depths 1 through RearRangeCells: directly behind, plus one cell on either side of each rear cell. Add a single-cell-wide ray directly left and directly right from the player's current cell, each extending SideRangeCells = ceil(RearRangeCells / 2). No forward cells or other floors qualify. Closed walls, closed gates and ordinary blocking geometry still block detection. Retain the selected monster while it qualifies; otherwise choose by shortest footprint depth, then smallest absolute lateral offset, then stable actor identity. On acquisition or replacement after the prior selection ceases to qualify, name the monster in a private BEHIND YOU, LEFT or RIGHT notice in the live die-readout and Die Log, play a clearly audible alert, and briefly show a violet directional light toward its position at detection. The light is a transient directional notification, not an enemy outline, minimap marker or persistent tracker. Do not repeat the alert while the same selected monster remains qualified. No target lock, aim assist, combat bonus, through-wall detection or AI behavior change.

rows.name: Killer Instinct
rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: While controlled by a human and wielding an equipped damage-dealing weapon, Killer Instinct remains dormant unless at least two living hostile actors are simultaneously inside the player's ordinary forward view and pass the same player-facing visibility/line-of-sight authority used for legal target identification. When that multi-hostile condition first becomes true and remains continuously true for 0.50 seconds, perform one target-priority evaluation; while it remains true, reevaluate no more than once every 1.00 second. If fewer than two valid hostiles remain, immediately clear the highlight and stop all Killer Instinct evaluation until the condition becomes true again; there is no general per-frame Think scan. Candidate discovery must reuse the existing visible/targetable hostile set or equivalent cached authority and may not iterate every world entity solely for this feat. For each valid candidate, compute a cheap deterministic EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot for one ordinary primary-fire trigger pull from the equipped weapon's current authored attack profile, using current deterministic attacker/target modifiers and mean damage-die values; do not roll dice, simulate Boom chains, predict future status procs, or Monte Carlo attacks. EstimatedShotsToKill = max(1, ceil(CurrentHP / max(1, EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot))). If one or more candidates have EstimatedShotsToKill = 1, select the one with the greatest EstimatedEffectiveDamagePerShot - CurrentHP kill margin; otherwise select the candidate with the lowest EstimatedShotsToKill. Break any remaining tie by lower CurrentHP, then stable actor ID. Render one red outline/halo tightly around the selected hostile model. The outline is informational only: it grants no aim assist, targeting lock, damage, AI-priority change, extra detection range, through-wall awareness, or tracking after ordinary visibility is lost, and it clears immediately when the target dies or becomes invalid.

rows.name: Omniscience
rows.actors: Heroes and human Soldiers
rows.effect: While controlled by a human, whenever this actor directly looks at a monster through the canonical look-at/target-identification trace, render an Omniscience readout above that monster at the same presentation anchor used for player identity text. For an ordinary AI monster, the readout shows the monster's canonical type/archetype name, current Combat Level, current class, and current Hit Points as CurrentHP/MaxHP. Example structure: Soldier • Level 21 • Fighter • HP 84/117. The values update live while the target remains valid. Omniscience is informational only: it grants no extra targeting range, no through-wall or off-screen awareness, no outline or tracking after look-away, and no combat/stat bonus. A human-controlled Soldier is still a monster for Omniscience purposes, but its existing HumanSoldierText remains the primary identity line; Omniscience appends the same Type/Level/Class/HP readout rather than replacing or hiding the controlling player's identity. Non-monster world entities and cooperative Heroes do not receive this monster-stat readout.

rows.name: Spellward
rows.actors: Heroes, human Soldiers, AI
rows.effect: Whenever the actor makes an otherwise-legal Magic Save, roll two sealed d20s, keep the higher natural result, then add the ordinary WIS and level modifiers once and compare with ordinary MagicDC. This is advantage, not a flat +2/+4/+6 bonus. It creates no save against an effect that normally supplies none. This single WIS 13 feat does not alter the separate INT Spellbreaker in the Arcane Disruption family.

rows.name: Sixth Sense
rows.actors: Cooperative heroes
rows.effect: Sixth Sense grants three personal perception effects. First, the owner can visually perceive any entity whose authoritative state includes invisible=true. Invisibility is a reusable shared entity-state primitive rather than a Watcher-specific exception: Watchers use it now, and future enemies, effects, or actors may use the same state. An invisible entity is rendered only for the owning client as a clearly readable translucent silhouette/outline at its true current world position whenever that entity would otherwise satisfy ordinary world visibility and line-of-sight rules if invisibility were ignored. Second, Sixth Sense grants Nearby Hostile Sense: every living hostile entity on the owner's current floor whose cell-coordinate distance is within 2 grid cells is rendered to that owner as a readable through-geometry outline even when intervening walls or props block line of sight. For this sensor, NearbyCellDistance = max(abs(enemyCellX-ownerCellX), abs(enemyCellY-ownerCellY)); the effect applies when NearbyCellDistance <= 2 and floorId matches. This local 5x5-cell neighborhood intentionally ignores wall connectivity and closed-gate edges for perception only. Invisible hostiles within that neighborhood are also revealed by the same outline. Third, Sixth Sense grants Watcher Motion Sense: whenever a living Watcher is in its authoritative moving/locomotion state, each Sixth Sense owner on the same floor receives a private 3D positional Watcher movement sound attached to that Watcher's true current position. This cue plays whether the Watcher is visible or invisible and does not require line of sight; ordinary spatial attenuation provides direction and proximity, so a distant Watcher does not become an all-floor audio beacon. The cue starts when authoritative Watcher locomotion begins and stops when locomotion stops, the Watcher dies/despawns, the player changes floor, or Sixth Sense is no longer active. The movement sound is transmitted/rendered only for eligible Sixth Sense owners; players without the feat receive no such sound event. These effects create no minimap marker, breadcrumb, directional arrow, nameplate through the world, aim assistance, target lock, ballistic permission through geometry, AI aggro knowledge, or interaction permission. Sixth Sense never changes an entity's invisible state, cloak duration, AI/state machine, collision, targetability rules, or visibility to any other player; players without the feat perceive the entity normally. The server authoritatively determines feat ownership, invisible state, hostility, floor, cell coordinates, and Watcher locomotion state; owning clients render only authorized silhouettes and private Watcher movement audio. FeatDirector may offer Sixth Sense whenever the actor is a cooperative hero who meets WIS 12; Watchers or any other invisibility-using enemy need not currently be present because the 2-cell hostile-sense effect is independently useful.

rows.name: Attunement
